simple_rule_metrics.label: Simple rule: purchase within 1 second of signup

stakeholder_findings.headline: Fraud risk ranking beats random, but accuracy is the wrong scorecard — and the strongest historical signal disappears in the future period.
key_data_insights: In the early (train) period, 7,600 purchases happen within 1 second of signup — and 100% of them are labeled fraud. That alone is 63% of train fraud.
In validation and test (later time), there are ZERO instant-signup purchases. The strongest train signal does not appear in the future window.
Fraud rate drops from ~11.4% (train) to ~4.6% (val/test). The problem is non-stationary.
Therefore a model that overfits the 'instant purchase' pattern looks strong on train and weak on locked future test.

simple_rule_train.rule: Flag if purchase within 1 second of signup
simple_rule_train.note: Perfect on historical burst fraud; useless on later period where that attack pattern is gone.

model_on_locked_test.interpretation: Top-k investigation queue is ~5× richer in fraud than random sampling. Overall accuracy is below the 95% majority baseline because the model trades false positives for fraud recall.

stakeholder_findings.why_accuracy_misleads: Always predicting 'normal' scores ~95% accuracy when fraud is only ~4.6% of test. A useful fraud system must surface risky cases for review; that increases false positives and lowers accuracy while improving ranking metrics (PR-AUC, Precision@k).
recommended_use: Use model scores to rank an investigation queue (Precision@k / enrichment), not as a hard automatic block at 0.5.
Do not judge success by accuracy alone.
Monitor concept drift: attack patterns (e.g. instant signup→buy) can vanish over time.
Retrain on recent windows; keep a locked chronological holdout for honest reporting.

operating_guidance.default: Rank by fraud probability; review top-N daily
operating_guidance.threshold_policy: Precision ≥ 0.50 was not achievable on the locked test PR curve for this model — max precision in useful recall range stays ~0.23. Prefer ranking + capacity-based top-N over a high precision cutoff.
